faqs.question: Is it okay to write Ram's name in a floor rangoli?
faqs.answer: Many families avoid it, because a name or image on the floor gets stepped on or swept up, so they put राम on a raised chowki, thali or wall instead. We found no published rule on this, so follow your household's custom; the five designs here keep the name and every figure off the walking floor.

faqs.question: What is the easiest Ram ji rangoli for a beginner?
faqs.answer: The bow-and-arrow strip: 9 by 5 dots at 2-inch spacing, three colours, about 210 g of powder and 20–25 minutes by our estimate. It is mostly arcs and straight lines, so a wobble reads as a bend in the bow rather than a mistake.

faqs.question: How much rangoli powder do I need for a Ram rangoli?
faqs.answer: By our estimates, from about 150 g for the 15-by-7.5-inch राम board to about 1.2 kg for the 30-by-36-inch temple. Buy a fifth more than you think you need, because outlines are always redrawn once.

faqs.question: How do I keep the letters of राम straight on a board?
faqs.answer: Draw the headline first along the top row of dots, then hang every stroke from it, because Devanagari letters hang from that line. Mark the dots in chalk at 1.25-inch spacing and outline in white before you fill anything.

faqs.question: Which colours suit a Ram ji rangoli?
faqs.answer: Saffron, white, red, yellow and green cover all five designs here, with blue added for the river in the ghat design. On white marble, outline in red instead of white so the lines stay visible.

faqs.question: How many diyas were lit at Ayodhya Deepotsav 2025?
faqs.answer: Guinness World Records lists 2,617,215 oil lamps at Deepotsav in Ayodhya on 19 October 2025, the current record for the largest display of oil lamps. They were lit within 25 minutes across 56 ghats.

faqs.question: Why do Ram's sandals appear in a rangoli?
faqs.answer: In the Ramayana, Bharat refuses the throne, carries Ram's gold-wrought sandals back from the forest and installs them on the royal seat, ruling in their name until Ram returns. Drawing the pair under a royal umbrella honours that loyalty without drawing Ram himself.

faqs.question: Can I use these designs for Ram Navami or Dussehra too?
faqs.answer: Yes. None of them is tied to a Diwali date; the ghat design is the most Diwali-specific because it borrows from Ayodhya's Deepotsav, held on the eve of Diwali.

faqs.question: How should I clear away a rangoli that has Ram's name on it?
faqs.answer: Many families lift the powder by hand or with a dry cloth rather than sweeping it into the bin, and tip it into a plant pot or garden soil. That is a custom, not a rule we could source, so do what your household does.

faqs.question: Does SubhSandesh have a tool for designing a Ram ji rangoli?
faqs.answer: No. Its Happy Diwali card has one rangoli scene, where the person you send it to colours a rangoli until your initials glow, but it cannot draw राम, set a dot grid or print a pattern.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Ram Ji Rangoli Designs: Five Dot-Grid Patterns With Steps

Ram ji rangoli designs work best when every motif comes from the Ramayana itself: Ram's bow, Bharat's sandals, Ayodhya's lamp-lit ghats, a temple shikhara, and the name राम on a raised board rather than the floor. Below are five original designs, each on a counted dot grid with size, colour count, powder weight and time, from a 20-minute bow strip to a 90-minute courtyard temple.

Plan the time before the pattern. In Raksha Bandhan 2026, the nearest festival SubhSandesh has measured (n = 89, not Diwali data), 49.4% of greeting pages were built on the festival day itself, and a rangoli left for Lakshmi Puja evening gets the same squeeze. And 48.3% of shared SubhSandesh pages are opened on a phone, so shoot your finished grid square-on from a chair or stair, where the dots line up on a small screen.

## What makes a rangoli a Ram ji rangoli?

A Ram ji rangoli is a floor or board design whose motifs come from the story of Ram's return to Ayodhya, the homecoming Diwali marks across north India. The motifs here are taken from Ralph Griffith's 1870–1874 English verse translation of Valmiki, which is [public domain on Project Gutenberg](https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/24869).

Three images in that text are drawable. Ram "broke the bow that bent to none" to win Sita; Bharat ruled through Ram's "gold-wrought sandals"; and Kausalya's lament in Book II pictures Ayodhya's royal street crowded with people throwing grain in welcome. Ayodhya's Deepotsav, on the eve of Diwali, adds a fourth: ghats lined with lamps.

## Where should Ram's name or image go? The floor custom

Many families keep Ram's name, face and figure off any floor where feet pass, because stepping on a deity's name or image is felt as disrespect. We found no published source stating this as a rule, so treat it as household custom, not scripture; your elders decide.

The designs follow that custom. The bow strip and ghat steps are symbols and sit at the doorstep; the राम board and the sandal pair go on a raised chowki or steel thali about 18 by 12 inches, since in Griffith's Book II Bharat installs the sandals "upon the royal seat". The temple sits in the courtyard inside a ring of diyas, and no design draws Ram's face.

## 5 Ram ji rangoli designs on dot grids, with sizes and colours

Each design gives grid, size, colours with powder, then time, followed by steps. Mark dots in chalk with a ruler; rows count from the top, columns from the left, and powder and time are our estimates (EST). For Diwali 2027, draw the doorstep designs on Choti Diwali, Thursday 28 October, so they are finished before Lakshmi Puja on Friday 29 October.

### 1. Dhanush-baan threshold strip

**Grid:** 9 dots across, 5 rows, 2 inches apart. **Size:** 16 by 8 inches. **Colours:** 3, saffron, white and green, about 210 g. **Time:** 20–25 minutes, beginner.

Lay the strip with row 1 nearest the door. Mark the bow tips at row 3, columns 1 and 9, and draw its back as one arc through row 2 column 3, row 1 column 5 and row 2 column 7. Draw the pulled string as a V from each tip to row 5, column 5.

Run the arrow from row 5, column 5 straight up, 2 inches past row 1, ending in a triangle pointing into the house. Add three green feather chevrons between rows 4 and 5, then double the bow line and fill it saffron.

### 2. राम naam on a raised board

**Grid:** 13 dots across, 7 rows, 1.25 inches apart, on a chowki or plank. **Size:** 15 by 7.5 inches. **Colours:** 3, white outline, yellow fill and a marigold-petal border, about 150 g. **Time:** 30 minutes, intermediate.

Draw the headline first along row 1, columns 1 to 13, because every Devanagari letter hangs from it. For र, drop a stroke from row 1, column 2 to row 3, curl it left to row 4, column 1, and sweep the tail to row 6, column 3. For the ा sign, draw a bar down column 5 to row 7.

For म, draw the stem down column 12 to row 7. Drop the left stroke from column 7 to row 3, curve it through row 4, column 9, and join the stem at row 4. Double each stroke 1 cm apart and fill yellow.

### 3. Saryu ghat steps with 25 diyas

**Grid:** 9 dots across, 6 rows, 3 inches apart. **Size:** 24 by 15 inches. **Colours:** 4, blue, white, ochre and orange, about 490 g, plus 25 clay diyas. **Time:** 45 minutes, intermediate.

Row 6 is the river: two wavy lines of dry rice, for the welcome grain, with blue between. Build the ghat as stepped ochre bands: row 5 across all nine columns, row 4 across columns 2–8, row 3 across 3–7, row 2 across 4–6, and one block at row 1, column 5.

Set a diya on every step dot: 9, 7, 5, 3 and 1, so 25 lamps, or draw orange flames. Keep lit diyas a hand's width from the edge and from any dupatta.

### 4. Bharat's paduka pair under a chhatra

**Grid:** 7 dots across, 9 rows, 2 inches apart, on a chowki or at the puja spot. **Size:** 12 by 16 inches. **Colours:** 3, gold-yellow, red and white, about 200 g. **Time:** 30–35 minutes, beginner.

Draw the royal umbrella as a red dome from row 1, column 4 down to row 3 at columns 1 and 7, dotting white along row 3 for the fringe. Below it, draw two upright ovals, columns 1–3 and 5–7, from row 4 to row 9. Add a 1-inch toe-knob at row 5 in each and fill the soles gold-yellow.

### 5. Shikhara with four flame niches

**Grid:** 11 dots across, 13 rows, 3 inches apart. **Size:** 30 by 36 inches. **Colours:** 5, white, saffron, red, yellow and green, about 1.2 kg. **Time:** about 90 minutes with two people, advanced.

Lay a green two-step plinth across rows 12 and 13, then the temple body from row 6 to row 11 across columns 2–10. In rows 8 to 10, draw four red arched niches centred on columns 3, 5, 7 and 9, each holding a yellow flame, the middle two taller.

The flames stand for Ram, Sita, Lakshman and Hanuman: a Ram darbar with no drawn face. Curve the saffron shikhara from row 6, columns 3 and 9, to a point at row 2, column 6, top it with a small kalash, and ring the plinth with 16 diyas.

## Grids, colours and powder compared for the five designs

The table sets the five side by side so you can choose by space and time; powder and time are estimates.

| Design | Dot grid | Finished size | Colours, powder (EST) | Time (EST) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Dhanush-baan strip | 9 × 5 at 2 in | 16 × 8 in | 3 colours, about 210 g | 20–25 min |
| 2. राम naam board | 13 × 7 at 1.25 in | 15 × 7.5 in | 3 colours, about 150 g plus petals | 30 min |
| 3. Saryu ghat steps | 9 × 6 at 3 in | 24 × 15 in | 4 colours, about 490 g, 25 diyas | 45 min |
| 4. Paduka under chhatra | 7 × 9 at 2 in | 12 × 16 in | 3 colours, about 200 g | 30–35 min |
| 5. Shikhara, four flames | 11 × 13 at 3 in | 30 × 36 in | 5 colours, about 1.2 kg | about 90 min |

Designs 1, 2 and 4 together need under 600 g and about 85 minutes, enough for a flat's doorway and a chowki. Design 5 alone needs twice that weight and two people.

## The Ayodhya Deepotsav numbers behind the ghat design

Guinness World Records lists the [largest display of oil lamps](https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/world-records/96019-largest-display-of-oil-lamps) as 2,617,215, set at Deepotsav in Ayodhya on 19 October 2025 by Uttar Pradesh's Department of Tourism and Dr. Rammanohar Lohia Avadh University. Lighting began at 17:30 IST and took 25 minutes across 56 ghats, with more than 30,000 university volunteers.

The 2024 edition had counted 2,512,585 lamps along the Saryu, per [Guinness's November 2024 report](https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/news/commercial/2024/11/showstopping-oil-lamp-records-broken-to-celebrate-diwali), which notes its guidelines no longer require every lamp to be lit. Your 25-diya ghat is roughly one hundred-thousandth of the 2025 figure.

One inconvenient detail: [UP Tourism's Deepotsav page](https://www.uptourism.gov.in/en/page/deepotsav), checked on 22 October 2026, still calls "over 12 lakhs diyas" at Ram ki Paidi last year's record. Caption your ghat with the Guinness figure, not that one.

## Sending your Ram rangoli to family who cannot see it

A rangoli reaches only people who cross your threshold, and lasts a day or two. For a grandmother in another city, SubhSandesh's [interactive Happy Diwali card](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-diwali) can carry it: she lights a diya at her door with a tag from you, lights a row of wish diyas, and colours a rangoli until your initials glow.

Up to six photos ride on its sky lanterns, so all five designs can go in. It opens in any browser with no app or account, takes about five minutes, and across SubhSandesh a page averages 11.1 views. It is not a rangoli designer: it cannot draw राम or set a grid.

If the person who taught you Ram bhajans is missing this Diwali, [Dedication, a radio show made for one person](https://subhsandesh.in/dedication), lets them tune through static to hear your voice introduce a bhajan. It is not a Diwali template.

## When a Ram ji rangoli, or SubhSandesh, is the wrong choice

At a society gate, even a symbol-only design is stepped on within hours; draw plain geometry there and keep the Ram motifs on your chowki. If your family avoids even the bow or sandals underfoot, move all five onto boards. With toddlers or pets around, 25 lit diyas at floor level is a fire risk, so use LED tealights.

SubhSandesh loses here too. It makes greeting pages, not floor art, and a phone photo flattens powder and petals. A grandparent without a smartphone gets nothing from a link; a printed 6-by-4 photo posted by Dhanteras, Wednesday 27 October 2027, reaches them better.

## Sources

- Guinness World Records, [Largest display of oil lamps](https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/world-records/96019-largest-display-of-oil-lamps), 19 October 2025.
- Guinness World Records, [Showstopping oil lamp records broken to celebrate Diwali](https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/news/commercial/2024/11/showstopping-oil-lamp-records-broken-to-celebrate-diwali), November 2024.
- UP Tourism, [Ayodhya Deepotsav](https://www.uptourism.gov.in/en/page/deepotsav), undated.
- Valmiki, [The Rámáyan of Válmíki](https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/24869), tr. Ralph T. H. Griffith, 1870–1874.

auditReport.honestAssessment: An answer engine has a reason to cite this over the measured top 10: it is the only result that turns Ram motifs into counted dot grids with sizes, colour counts, powder and time, ties each motif to a quoted line of Valmiki, gives the Guinness-verified 2025 Deepotsav count while flagging that UP Tourism's page is stale, and addresses where Ram's name should sit. Its weaknesses: the query is overwhelmingly visual and the SERP is Pinterest and YouTube, the post has no drawings of its own (text grids only), quantities are estimates, the floor custom is unsourced, and a low-authority domain should expect months, not weeks.
